about.title: Windsor Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Windsor's economy mixes agriculture, hospitality, and small manufacturing, and workers in each of these fields face real injury risks — from vineyard equipment to delivery routes along Old Redwood Highway and US-101. When a workplace injury happens, California generally routes the claim through workers' compensation, regardless of who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that helps injured Windsor workers get in touch with an independent attorney who can look at the details of what happened and explain the options available. There's no cost to connect, and no obligation to move forward.

items.title: Third-Party Claims May Apply
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker contributed to your injury, a separate claim may be available.

items.title: Deadlines Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and third-party claims carry a 2-year filing deadline under California law, so timing can affect your options.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report an injury or file a claim, and an attorney can help explain your protections if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Old Redwood Highway — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the first path since it's usually the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault. However, if a third party like a subcontractor, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to the accident, a separate injury claim may also be possible. An independent attorney can review the specifics and explain which paths apply to your situation.

items.question: What if my employer in Windsor tries to punish me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: California law makes retaliation against injured workers illegal, whether that's termination, demotion, or reduced hours. If you believe you're facing retaliation after reporting a workplace injury, it's worth speaking with an independent attorney who can review what happened. LawProactive can help connect you with one at no cost.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. If a third party is involved, that type of claim typically carries a 2-year deadline under California law. Because timing matters, it helps to get information early even if you're still deciding how to proceed.
